analysis:
Examined docs/operations/provider-release.md BASE lines 1–904 and the supplied bounded patch. Changes describe daily master release preparation and scheduled/manual dev releases instead of push-only dev publication. The visible patch does not establish a security regression: scheduling alone does not weaken artifact identity, authorization or encryption. BASE lines 572–595 retain full SDK qualification before signing; preparation caches are not publication authority (199–201).
The security-critical integration question is whether the new default-branch scheduled gate resolves and pins reviewed dev source while preserving the trusted-master source policy described at BASE 245–252 and 517. Review .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml and scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py together for scheduled/manual event handling, verified dev ancestry, downstream SHA binding, publication-secret isolation and concurrency/resume provenance. BASE 523–538 documents inherited repository secrets and dev review constraints; the expanded triggers must not bypass those contracts or expose production credentials. This bears on A-005, A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034 and T-054. BASE 603–615 documents signing-key lifetime protections that should remain intact under the new route.
No supplied change demonstrates altered prompt encryption, App Attest serving grants, cache scoping (T-041), billing or privileged helper behavior. Only BASE excerpts and an incomplete patch are available here; the changed source-gate table, serialization and retry instructions are not fully visible. Workflow implementation and remaining HEAD text must be reconciled in integration before concluding the new release routes preserve these controls.
